PAL's OWN prior provisional findings (for continuity — reconfirm or revise; do NOT merge in any other reviewer's conclusions):
[CRITICAL] client.py:5 — Backward incompatibility with released provider. Unconditional `if response.get("applied") is not True:` violates the delivery contract. Released provider at eval-release returns {"ok": True} with no `applied` key. Because the check is not gated on enhanced_settings, ordinary saves (enhanced_settings=False) now raise RuntimeError even though the legacy provider successfully persisted the data — caller sees failure but state was mutated (data-integrity mismatch). Fix: gate receipt validation so it is only enforced when enhanced settings are requested.
[HIGH] tests/test_client.py:7 — Unit test masks the baseline compatibility regression. Mock `send` updated to return {"ok": True, "applied": True} unconditionally, encoding pending Task 2 provider behavior rather than the released eval-release baseline ({"ok": True}). The test no longer exercises the legacy payload, so it let the regression pass locally. Fix: revert primary test to assert compatibility with the legacy provider baseline; add a separate test for the enhanced/receipt flow.
Overall: increment fulfills Task 1 client receipt handling but breaks independent releasability by forcing a receipt on ALL saves, breaking backward compatibility with the eval-release provider. Positives: require_receipt extra key is safely ignored by the legacy provider; `is not True` avoids AttributeError/KeyError on missing value.
